figures.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram. Create ONE original wide horizontal README illustration, target 1920 by 640 pixels, approximately 3:1. Purpose: show at a glance what the GitHub Manager demo site contains. A calm, friendly hand-drawn sketchbook illustration on pure white paper: slightly irregular dark navy pen outlines, readable large handwritten headings, recognizable semantic objects, generous whitespace. Indigo #3949AB and blue #1E69D6 accents, soft light-blue and lavender marker washes, very restrained purple. Match the project’s approachable paper-and-marker technical explanation style. Keep it MUCH simpler than a full architecture diagram.
Composition: three equally weighted isolated illustrated vignettes across a single row. NO enclosing panels, no connecting arrows, no numbered sequence, no busy backgrounds. These are independent destinations, not processing steps. Left: an open laptop showing a sparse repository-list interface and an obvious triangular video play badge. Center: an open architecture notebook or blueprint with a simple connected three-part sketch and a pair of headphones beside it, conveying video/audio design explanation. Right: a small illustrated storyboard of a source document, magnifying glass and organized label cards with a small play badge, conveying animated illustrated system design. Objects are large and immediately recognizable, never technical service-name boxes.
Only visible text, exactly these three headings, one under each vignette: "App walkthrough", "Architecture deep dive", "Illustrated system design". Wrap a heading to two balanced lines if needed. Make all lettering large enough to be clear when the full image displays at 850px width. No other words, no tiny UI text, no fake data or metrics, no footer, no title repeated at the top, no watermark. Leave generous edge margins and ample empty white paper between objects. This is an orientation thumbnail, not an exhaustive feature map.

Use case: infographic-diagram. Create ONE original wide horizontal README illustration, target 1920 by 640 pixels, approximately 3:1. Purpose: preview the GitHub Manager plain-language ground-truth evaluation article. Calm friendly hand-drawn sketchbook style on pure white paper: slightly irregular dark navy pen outlines, large readable handwritten headings, recognizable semantic objects, generous whitespace. Indigo #3949AB and blue #1E69D6 accents with light-blue and lavender marker washes and restrained purple for the human review step. Keep it simple, professional, and visually consistent with a paper-and-marker technical explainer.
Single left-to-right three-stop visual story with two slender hand-drawn directional arrows: LEFT, a small stack of repository README documents and two folder tabs, representing a saved public repository corpus. CENTER, one friendly human reviewer examining a clipboard containing a few distinct rounded label chips, representing human confirmation for a SMALL SUBSET of the corpus. RIGHT, a magnifying glass inspecting two aligned lists with check marks and one small visibly missed item, representing comparing retrieval/classification outputs against reviewed labels. Do not use a bar chart with fabricated values. No robot as judge, no trophy, no perfect-score claims.
Only visible text, exactly these three headings, one above or below each main group: "600 public repos", "30 reviewed repos", "Measured evaluation". The first arrow means selecting a reviewed subset, NOT that all 600 were human validated. The second arrow means comparison with human reference labels, NOT human labels fed into the classifier. Do not draw human labels flowing into a robot, model, or prompt. Keep those semantics through the objects; do not add explanatory sentences to the image. No accuracy percentage, no invented statistics, no extra words, no footer, no overall title, no watermark. Large objects and lettering that remain clear at 850px display width; generous clean margins and open whitespace. No enclosing panels or dense block diagrams.
